## Strategy

**Hypotheses and definitions.** Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) be bigrassmannian, with \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Put
\[
q=n-r,\quad i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad
a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j).
\]
Let \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\) be the integral symmetric-function ring with Schur basis \(\{s_\lambda\}\),
\[
I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,\quad
A=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\quad A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d,
\]
\[
J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda\subseteq A,
\qquad Q=J_v/A_+J_v.
\]
For \(a=0\), \(b^a\) has the unique empty partition, declared self-complementary.

**Dependencies.** The lower-family integral-basis certificate is `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1`. Integral quotient conjugation is `research-attempt-research-plan-task-301-1`; its application to the right family is `research-attempt-research-plan-task-286-1`. The Hilbert-series and perfect-pairing consequences are `research-attempt-research-plan-task-317-1`. DOI lines 219–235 give the lower-family theorem and generation statement; DOI lines 819–825 give the no-syzygy mechanism.

**Consolidated proof.** Let
\[
G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\},\qquad
G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}.
\]
The source supplies generation of \(J_v\) by \(G_L\) [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]. By `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1`, a homogeneous kernel element of the induced graded surjection \(\mathbb Z[G_L]\twoheadrightarrow Q\) gives a nonzero source-form syzygy. The no-syzygy theorem excludes it [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-825], including the separately handled \(a=0\) boundary. Hence \(G_L\) is a homogeneous integral basis of \(Q\).

By `research-attempt-research-plan-task-301-1` and `research-attempt-research-plan-task-286-1`, partition conjugation gives an integral graded isomorphism to the conjugate-parameter quotient and carries \(G_R(v)\) bijectively to the lower family there. Thus \(G_R\) is also a homogeneous integral basis of \(Q\). A proper subfamily of either basis cannot generate \(Q\), hence cannot generate \(J_v\); both families are minimal.

Indexing the lower basis by \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) yields
\[
Q\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Ze_\rho,\qquad
\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|,\qquad
H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z.
\]
Thus \(Q\) is torsion-free. Complementation
\[
\rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1)
\]
gives the perfect integral pairing
\[
\langle e_\rho,e_\sigma\rangle=\delta_{\sigma,\rho^\vee}:
Q_d\times Q_{2ij+ab-d}\to\mathbb Z.
\]

**Verdict.** The requested theorem boundary is established. No transition-matrix or finite-computation claim is used.
